title: Getting started with parametricboot
text: Standard errors confidence intervals regression models usually rest large-sample approximations. parametric bootstrap checks, necessary replaces, approximations simulation: fit model data; simulate new response fitted model, keeping covariates fixed; refit model simulated response; repeat steps 2 3 many times. data-generating mechanism step 2 known exactly (fitted model), spread refitted estimates around original one shows estimator behaves samples like : whether biased, variable , whether textbook intervals achieve nominal coverage. parametricboot runs loop lm(), glm(), lme4::lmer(), lme4::glmer() survival::coxph() fits, provides tools summarise result.
code: library(parametricboot)

title: Getting started with parametricboot
text: Collett (1991) describes experiment batches 20 tobacco budworm moths sex exposed six doses pyrethroid. response number moths killed. pb_simulate() draws replicates. seed, result reproducible session’s random number stream left untouched. model refitted re-evaluating call original data, two-column response log2(dose) term need special treatment. requirement model fitted data argument.
code: budworm <- data.frame(   sex = rep(c("M", "F"), each = 6),   dose = rep(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), times = 2),   dead = c(1, 4, 9, 13, 18, 20, 0, 2, 6, 10, 12, 16),   n = 20 ) fit <- glm(cbind(dead, n - dead) ~ sex + log2(dose), data = budworm, family = binomial()) res <- pb_simulate(fit, n = 500, seed = 2025) res #> <pb_boot> Parametric bootstrap #>   Model:      glm (binomial) #>   Replicates: 500 #>   Terms:      (Intercept), sexM, log2(dose)

title: Getting started with parametricboot
text: pb_predict_boot() returns one column predictions per replicate; extra arguments go predict(). pb_plot_predictions() whole grid plots result:
code: new_moths <- data.frame(sex = c("M", "F"), dose = 8) preds <- pb_predict_boot(res, new_moths, type = "response") dim(preds) #> [1]   2 500 t(apply(preds, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))) #>        2.5%       50%     97.5% #> 1 0.5864280 0.6950555 0.8019143 #> 2 0.3161773 0.4301403 0.5545194 males <- data.frame(sex = "M", dose = seq(1, 32, length.out = 100)) pb_plot_predictions(res, males, x = "dose", type = "response")

title: Getting started with parametricboot
text: Refits throw error dropped, refits raise warnings counted rather printed one one. reported single warning, second kind deserves attention. Consider logistic regression 32 rows mtcars: simulated data sets two groups perfectly separated mpg. maximum likelihood estimate exist data, glm() returns whatever huge value iterations stopped . handful replicates dominates every mean standard deviation: pb_drop_warned() excludes replicates raised warnings: reveals genuine, substantial, small-sample bias logistic regression: coefficients overestimated absolute value fifth. Two caveats apply. cleaned summaries conditional fit well behaved. Report proportion dropped replicates . Percentile intervals far less sensitive means: quantile registers replicates extreme, much. need treatment, arguably honest without : Replicates never dropped automatically, every warning signals useless fit. res$warned flags affected replicates can inspect res$replicates deciding.
code: small <- glm(vs ~ mpg, data = mtcars, family = binomial()) res_small <- pb_simulate(small, n = 500, seed = 2025) #> Warning: 6 of 500 bootstrap refits produced warnings (for example convergence #> problems). pb_key_stats(res_small)[c("term", "estimate", "bias", "std_error")] #>          term   estimate       bias std_error #> 1 (Intercept) -8.8330726 -4.9004163 44.752399 #> 2         mpg  0.4304135  0.2487127  2.278504 clean <- pb_drop_warned(res_small) clean #> <pb_boot> Parametric bootstrap #>   Model:      glm (binomial) #>   Replicates: 500 (6 dropped) #>   Terms:      (Intercept), mpg pb_key_stats(clean)[c("term", "estimate", "bias", "std_error")] #>          term   estimate        bias std_error #> 1 (Intercept) -8.8330726 -1.80982691 4.4722676 #> 2         mpg  0.4304135  0.09165097 0.2235875 pb_confint(res_small) #>          term   estimate       lower     upper #> 1 (Intercept) -8.8330726 -25.2280569 -4.829614 #> 2         mpg  0.4304135   0.2393271  1.296134 pb_confint(clean) #>          term   estimate       lower     upper #> 1 (Intercept) -8.8330726 -23.1226342 -4.823974 #> 2         mpg  0.4304135   0.2388539  1.131722

title: Getting started with parametricboot
text: ‘lme4’ models, new random effects drawn every replicate summaries refer fixed effects. Refitting mixed models slow, pb_parallel() pays : takes arguments pb_simulate(), plus workers, returns identical result given seed. Pass re.form = NA pb_predict_boot() population-level predictions.
code: cbpp <- lme4::cbpp gm <- lme4::glmer(   cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd),   data = cbpp, family = binomial() )  res_gm <- pb_simulate(gm, n = 100, seed = 1) #> boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') # Equivalent, on two cores: pb_parallel(gm, n = 100, workers = 2, seed = 1)  pb_summary_table(res_gm) #>          term  estimate  boot_mean          bias std_error        mse coverage #> 1 (Intercept) -1.398343 -1.4082260 -0.0098830876 0.2281372 0.05162379     0.96 #> 2     period2 -0.991925 -0.9926646 -0.0007395901 0.2867139 0.08138338     0.97 #> 3     period3 -1.128216 -1.1266335  0.0015827549 0.3720195 0.13701701     0.94 #> 4     period4 -1.579745 -1.6396247 -0.0598793034 0.4260859 0.18331925     0.96 #>       lower      upper #> 1 -1.831125 -0.9797858 #> 2 -1.612817 -0.5969268 #> 3 -1.920486 -0.5743643 #> 4 -2.608564 -0.9305711

title: Getting started with parametricboot
text: Cox model leaves baseline hazard censoring mechanism unspecified, fully parametric model simulate . coxph fits, pb_simulate() uses model-based resampling algorithm Davison Hinkley (1997, Algorithm 7.3): failure times drawn fitted survivor function Ŝ0(t)exp⁡(x⊤β̂)\hat S_0(t)^{\exp(x^\top\hat\beta)}, Ŝ0\hat S_0 based Breslow estimate baseline hazard; subjects censored keep censoring time, others get censoring time drawn Kaplan-Meier estimate censoring distribution, conditional exceeding observed time. right-censored, unweighted models without strata(), tt() penalised terms supported. bootstrap standard errors close partial-likelihood ones, shown , Wald intervals close nominal coverage, reassuring. keep_fits = FALSE stores estimates, saves memory need predictions.

title: Parametric Bootstrap for Fitted Regression Models
text: classic dose-response experiment (Collett, 1991): batches 20 tobacco budworm moths sex exposed six doses pyrethroid, number killed recorded. 12 binomial observations, far can large-sample theory behind summary(fit) trusted? pb_summary_table() reports, coefficient, bootstrap estimates bias, standard error mean squared error, actual coverage nominal 95% Wald interval, bootstrap confidence interval: news good: slope overestimated 2%, small fraction standard error, Wald intervals cover advertised. bootstrap distributions close normal:  replicates give intervals prediction, dose-response curve male moths:
code: library(parametricboot)  budworm <- data.frame(   sex = rep(c("M", "F"), each = 6),   dose = rep(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), times = 2),   dead = c(1, 4, 9, 13, 18, 20, 0, 2, 6, 10, 12, 16),   n = 20 ) fit <- glm(cbind(dead, n - dead) ~ sex + log2(dose), data = budworm, family = binomial())  res <- pb_simulate(fit, n = 1000, seed = 2025) res #> <pb_boot> Parametric bootstrap #>   Model:      glm (binomial) #>   Replicates: 1000 #>   Terms:      (Intercept), sexM, log2(dose) pb_summary_table(res) #>          term  estimate boot_mean        bias std_error        mse coverage #> 1 (Intercept) -3.473155 -3.552493 -0.07933778 0.4839494 0.24026729    0.954 #> 2        sexM  1.100743  1.117377  0.01663401 0.3784177 0.14333343    0.945 #> 3  log2(dose)  1.064214  1.088388  0.02417447 0.1352250 0.01885192    0.946 #>        lower     upper #> 1 -4.5809602 -2.702189 #> 2  0.4015961  1.856280 #> 3  0.8444751  1.401441 pb_plot_estimates(res) males <- data.frame(sex = "M", dose = seq(1, 32, length.out = 100)) pb_plot_predictions(res, males, x = "dose", type = "response")

title: Drop replicates whose refit raised a warning — pb_drop_warned
text: typical use logistic regression small samples, simulated data sets perfectly separated. maximum likelihood estimate exist data: glm() warns fitted probabilities 0 1 occurred returns arbitrary, large coefficients. handful replicates enough ruin bootstrap means, standard errors histograms. Dropping changes question answered: summaries describe estimator conditional fit well behaved. Report proportion dropped replicates alongside results. Percentile intervals pb_confint() barely affected extreme replicates need treatment. every warning signals useless fit (mixed models, convergence warnings often false alarms), replicates never dropped automatically. Inspect results$warned affected results$replicates deciding.

title: Drop replicates whose refit raised a warning — pb_drop_warned
code: # About 1% of data sets simulated from this model are perfectly separated fit <- glm(vs ~ mpg, data = mtcars, family = binomial()) res <- suppressWarnings(pb_simulate(fit, n = 300, seed = 2025)) sum(res$warned) #> [1] 4  pb_key_stats(res)[c("term", "bias", "std_error")] #>          term       bias std_error #> 1 (Intercept) -6.5026028 57.581787 #> 2         mpg  0.3300858  2.931462 pb_key_stats(pb_drop_warned(res))[c("term", "bias", "std_error")] #>          term       bias std_error #> 1 (Intercept) -1.5726316 4.4847282 #> 2         mpg  0.0800258 0.2217842

title: Roadmap
text: pb_simulate() – run N parametric bootstrap replicates, lm(), glm(), lme4::lmer(), lme4::glmer() survival::coxph() fits. pb_parallel() – run refits parallel (base ‘parallel’ cluster), reproducibly. pb_drop_warned() – exclude replicates whose refit raised warning (example separated logistic regressions). pb_key_stats() – bias, standard error, MSE Wald coverage. pb_confint() – percentile, basic normal intervals. pb_summary_table(), pb_tidy(), print(), summary() confint() methods. pb_plot_estimates(), pb_plot_diagnostics(), pb_plot_predictions(). pb_predict_boot() – predictions bootstrap uncertainty. pb_compare_models() – bootstrap distribution fit criterion. pb_resample() – case-resampling helper. Ideas later versions: Studentised (bootstrap-t) intervals, using stored standard errors. Bootstrap likelihood-ratio test nested models, pbkrtest::PBmodcomp(). Bootstrap distributions variance components mixed models. coxph models strata(). ‘future’ backend pb_parallel() (clusters, progress reporting). ‘broom’-style tidy() glance() methods.

title: parametricboot 0.0.0.9000
text: pb_simulate() rewritten. previous implementation refit model: inside replicate(), ... referred replicate counter, passed update() formula. Models refitted original data rather model frame, formulas transformed terms (log(x), poly(x, 2)), offset(), weights, subset, y ~ . two-column binomial responses work, fits rows dropped missing values. lm() lme4::lmer() models now supported alongside glm() lme4::glmer(). Mixed models refitted lme4::refit() summarised fixed effects. survival::coxph() models, simulate() method exists, bootstrapped model-based resampling algorithm Davison Hinkley (1997, Algorithm 7.3). Stratified, weighted, penalised counting-process models rejected informative error. New seed argument reproducible results leave global random number generator untouched, keep_fits argument store estimates. Refits fail dropped refits raise warnings counted; reported single warning instead aborting flooding console. New pb_drop_warned() excludes replicates whose refit raised warning, example perfectly separated data sets small logistic regressions generate, whose arbitrary huge coefficients otherwise ruin bootstrap means standard errors. pb_parallel() shares engine pb_simulate() returns identical results given seed. validates model, defaults 2 workers instead cores, checks workers can load package.

title: parametricboot 0.0.0.9000
text: pb_key_stats() gains estimate, boot_mean std_error columns. coverage now estimated coverage Wald interval (used logical flag TRUE construction). New level argument. pb_confint() gains type = c("percentile", "basic", "normal") estimate column. pb_summary_table() keeps coefficients model order gains level type arguments. pb_tidy() returns base data frame; ‘tidyr’ dependency gone. pb_compare_models() now evaluates metric bootstrap refits reports mean, standard deviation percentile interval (used bootstrap model discard replicates). Models can named. New print(), summary() confint() methods pb_boot objects.

title: parametricboot 0.0.0.9000
text: pb_plot_estimates() draws histograms original estimate marked (used overlay kernel density single point), pb_plot_diagnostics() adds running mean. , parameter now optional defaults coefficients. pb_plot_predictions() shows predictions row newdata bootstrap percentile intervals, instead one pooled density. parameter argument replaced x, level new. pb_predict_boot() passes ... predict() always returns matrix.
